Looking at the image, the right hand is holding the blue Joy-Con on the right side of the console. To remove a Joy-Con from the Switch, you slide it outward, perpendicular to the console's edge. The Joy-Con is attached on the right side, so to remove it, you slide it to the right (away from the console).

Now I need to look at the colored arrows. There's a coordinate system overlay with four arrows:
- Yellow arrow pointing up
- Green arrow pointing right
- Blue arrow pointing left
- Red arrow pointing down

The blue Joy-Con is on the right side of the console. To disconnect it, the right hand should move it to the right, which corresponds to the green arrow.

Let me double check the orientation. The console is lying flat (or at an angle) on the table. The blue controller is on the right edge. The green arrow points to the right, which is the outward direction for the right Joy-Con.

Thus the answer is B (green).

Let me confirm by considering the axes. The red arrow points down (toward the bottom of the screen), yellow up, green right, blue left. The right Joy-Con slides off to the right side. So green.

Therefore the answer is B.
